skill.summary: Refactor code incrementally while preserving tested behavior.

content.user_title: Refactor Code Safely with Test-Driven Workflows
content.value_statement: Large refactors can introduce regressions and obscure whether performance improved. This skill structures small changes around tests, measurements, design principles, and recovery steps.
actual_capabilities: Establishes a passing test baseline before refactoring begins.
Identifies common code smells and suggests focused refactoring techniques.
Organizes changes into small steps with tests after each modification.
Applies SOLID principles and design patterns when they provide clear value.
Compares coverage, performance, and test results before and after changes.
Provides recovery guidance when a refactoring step breaks tests.
limitations: Requires an existing codebase and runnable tests for reliable validation.
Does not provide a bundled test runner, profiler, or mutation testing tool.
Cannot guarantee behavior preservation when test coverage is incomplete.
Requires project-specific review before applying architecture or performance recommendations.

use_cases.title: Improve a Legacy Module
use_cases.description: Create an incremental plan for reducing duplication and long methods while keeping existing tests green.

use_cases.title: Review a Refactoring Proposal
use_cases.description: Assess planned structural changes against SOLID principles, coverage, performance evidence, and rollback needs.

use_cases.title: Teach the Refactor Phase
use_cases.description: Demonstrate how small behavior-preserving changes follow a passing test baseline.

prompt_templates.title: Plan a Small Refactor
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this function for code smells. Propose one small refactoring step and explain which tests should pass afterward: [function and tests].
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning a focused behavior-preserving change

prompt_templates.title: Extract Responsibilities
prompt_templates.prompt: Refactor this class incrementally while preserving behavior. Identify responsibilities, propose extraction steps, and run relevant tests after each step: [class and tests].

prompt_templates.title: Improve Performance Safely
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze this measured bottleneck. Propose a tested optimization, define before-and-after metrics, and separate structural changes from behavior changes: [profile and code].
prompt_templates.scenario: Experienced developer optimizing a tested component

prompt_templates.title: Evolve a Legacy Architecture
prompt_templates.prompt: Design an incremental migration for this legacy subsystem. Use tests, interface boundaries, compatibility stages, performance checks, and a rollback plan: [architecture context].
prompt_templates.scenario: Technical lead planning a large refactoring program

output_examples.input: Refactor an order processor that validates orders, calculates totals, and coordinates payment in one method.
output: Baseline: run order validation, total calculation, payment failure, and inventory failure tests.
Plan: extract validation and total calculation before introducing service boundaries.
Verification: run focused tests after each extraction, then run the full suite and compare timing.

output_examples.input: Reduce repeated database queries in a tested product listing service.
output_examples.output: Measure query counts first, add a regression test, introduce batched loading, rerun tests, and compare latency and query totals.

best_practices: Start from a passing test baseline and record relevant coverage and performance metrics.
Make one focused structural change at a time and rerun the smallest relevant test set.
Keep behavior changes separate from refactoring commits and verify the full suite before completion.
anti_patterns: Do not apply design patterns without a specific problem they solve.
Do not combine broad architecture changes, feature work, and performance optimization in one step.
Do not treat passing tests as sufficient when coverage misses important behavior.

faq.question: Does this skill write tests before every refactor?
faq.answer: It first checks the existing safety net and recommends focused tests when important behavior lacks coverage.

faq.question: Can it refactor code without an existing test suite?
faq.answer: It can propose a plan, but reliable behavior preservation requires tests or another trusted verification method.

faq.question: Which programming languages does it support?
faq.answer: The workflow is language independent, although the included before-and-after example uses TypeScript.

faq.question: Does it automatically run project commands?
faq.answer: The skill describes when to run tests and measurements. Actual command selection depends on the project and available tools.

faq.question: Will every refactor improve performance?
faq.answer: No. Performance changes require measured bottlenecks and before-and-after comparisons.

faq.question: How should failed refactoring steps be handled?
faq.answer: Stop, identify the breaking change, restore the last known passing state, and retry with a smaller step.
